parse_error_station.title: MeteoSwiss station file format changed
parse_error_station.description: The SwissMetNet station observation file could not be parsed. The upstream format may have changed. Check `docs/ogd.md` in the integration repository for the current format and open a drift issue if the layout no longer matches.

parse_error_forecast.title: MeteoSwiss forecast file format changed
parse_error_forecast.description: The local forecast file could not be parsed. The upstream format may have changed. Check `docs/ogd.md` in the integration repository for the current format and open a drift issue if the layout no longer matches.

user.title: MeteoSwiss Weather
user.description: Set up the official MeteoSwiss open data integration. Choose the type of forecast location.

data_description.forecast_mode: Postal code for a town or city; mountain point for a summit, pass, or resort.

postal_code.title: Postal code
postal_code.description: Enter your Swiss postal code. The value is pre-filled from your Home Assistant location.

data_description.postal_code: Swiss postal code (PLZ) of the place to forecast.

mountain.title: Select mountain point
mountain.description: Choose the mountain summit, pass, or resort to forecast. The nearest point to your Home Assistant location is pre-selected.

point.title: Select forecast point
point.description: This postal code has more than one forecast point. Select the one you want.

station.title: Select weather station
station.description: Choose the SwissMetNet station to use for current conditions. The nearest station is pre-selected.{radar_hint}

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure MeteoSwiss Weather
reconfigure.description: Change the forecast location type and weather station without deleting the entry. The current type is pre-selected.

data_description.forecast_mode: Postal code for a town or city; mountain point for a summit, pass, or resort.

history.title: Weather station changed
history.description: You changed the weather station from {old_station} to {new_station}. Choose what to do with the history recorded so far. Backfill affects long-term statistics only, not the raw short-term states.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the MeteoSwiss open data service. Check your network and try again.
error.unknown_postal_code: No forecast point found for this postal code. Check the code and try again.

abort.already_configured: This forecast point is already configured.
abort.no_mountain_points: No mountain forecast points are available in the metadata.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The MeteoSwiss Weather entry was updated.

options.keep: Keep the recorded history (values so far came from the previous station; the switch is logged)
options.discard: Discard: purge the station sensors' states and clear their long-term statistics for a clean start
options.backfill: Backfill: rewrite the long-term statistics from the new station's official history

import_history.name: Import history
import_history.description: Imports the configured station's official hourly history into Home Assistant's long-term statistics (mean/min/max temperature, mean for humidity, dew point, pressure, wind and radiation, hourly sum for precipitation). Long-term statistics only, not raw states. Overlapping periods are replaced, not duplicated. This is a one-off download outside the recurring traffic budget: about 1 MB for the current year, 8-13 MB per past decade, about 45 MB for everything since 1980.

config_entry_id.name: Integration entry
config_entry_id.description: The MeteoSwiss Weather config entry whose station history to import.

start.name: Start
start.description: Earliest time to import (local time when no timezone is given). Defaults to 1 January of the current year.

end.name: End
end.description: Latest time to import (local time when no timezone is given). Defaults to now.

data_description.hourly_forecast: The hourly forecast is fetched with HTTP Range requests, so the cost depends on the horizon you pick next. Refreshed at most every 3 hours. Disabled by default to stay within the fair-use traffic budget.

hourly.title: Hourly forecast horizon
hourly.description: How far ahead to fetch the hourly forecast, counted in full local calendar days. A shorter horizon downloads less. "Full run" fetches all ~220 hours (about 9 days).

data_description.hourly_horizon_days: Default: the rest of today plus two full days (about 7–11 MB per refresh). "Full run" fetches every hour (about 30 MB per refresh).
